claim: The Hermitage hillside has signposted walking paths up through the terraced vineyards to the Chapelle Saint-Christophe at the summit, with the 'Sur les Pas de Gambert, en Hermitage' interpretive trail explaining the terroir.
quote: Sur les Pas de Gambert, en Hermitage… an informative track across the hillside… The summit snack… The ascent is not hard… but still makes your calves warm up

claim: The Chapelle Saint-Christophe sits at 329 m elevation above Tain and gives a panoramic view over the Drôme and Rhône valley; a Roman temple to Hercules once stood on the site.
quote: Chapelle Saint-Christophe… 329 metres… built in 1864 on a site believed to have previously housed a Roman temple dedicated to Hercules

claim: From the Taurobole square in central Tain, the walk up to the Saint-Christophe chapel takes about 45 minutes; alternatively you can drive to the Pierre Aiguille belvedere and reach the chapel on foot in 10 minutes.
quote: a simple walk up to the chapel from the Taurobole Square in Tain, taking about 45 minutes… drive to the Pierre Aiguille lookout and walk to the chapel in about 10 minutes

claim: Cité du Chocolat Valrhona in Tain-l'Hermitage is open Mon 10:00–12:00 / 13:00–18:30, Tue–Sat 09:00–12:00 / 13:00–18:30, and Sun/holidays 10:00–12:00 / 13:00–17:30, closed only 1 Jan, 1 May and 25 Dec.
quote: Monday: 10am - 12pm and 1pm - 6:30pm, Tuesday to Saturday: 9am - 12pm and 1pm - 6:30pm, and Sunday and holidays: 10am - 12pm and 1pm - 5:30pm

claim: The Marc Seguin footbridge linking Tain-l'Hermitage to Tournon-sur-Rhône was built 1847–1849 and is the oldest suspension bridge in France still in service, classed as a historic monument in 1985.
quote: Marc Seguin Bridge (Tournon-sur-Rhône/Tain-L'Hermitage, 1849)… oldest suspension bridge in France still in service

claim: Marc Seguin and his brothers built the world's first wire-cable suspension bridge over the Rhône between Tournon and Tain in 1825, predating the current pedestrian span by two decades.
quote: In 1825, Seguin and his four younger brothers built the world's first suspension bridge in which the roadway was suspended from wire cables; it was erected over the Rhône river between Tournon and Tain l'Hermitage

claim: The Château-Musée de Tournon-sur-Rhône is open daily 18 March–1 November 2026, with afternoon-only hours (14:00–18:00) in May and June; full-price ticket €5, reduced €4.
quote: March 18 to November 1, 2026… May 2 to June 30: daily from 2 pm to 6 pm… full price €5, reduced price €4

claim: The Train de l'Ardèche steam train departs from Saint-Jean-de-Muzols just outside Tournon and runs into the Gorges du Doux, with the full-day 'Mastrou' service leaving Tournon at 10:15 and returning at 17:00 between April and late October.
quote: 10:15 am departure from Tournon St Jean by steam train, 11:00 am arrival at Boucieu le Roi… 4:15 pm departure from Boucieu le Roi by steam train for the return journey, ending at 5:00 pm

claim: Paul Jaboulet Aîné's Vineum in Tain offers three tasting formats — by-the-glass with charcuterie/cheese, paired with the chef's dishes, or as a guided educational session — and can be combined with a walk up to the Chapelle de l'Hermitage vineyard.
quote: the pleasure version with wine by the glass accompanied by charcuterie and cheese, the gourmet version with the Chef's dishes, or the educational version during guided tasting sessions

claim: The M. Chapoutier tasting cellar at 18 avenue du Dr Paul Durand in Tain-l'Hermitage is open roughly Mon afternoon–Sat 10:00–12:00 / 14:00–18:00 (Sat to 17:00); reservations on +33 4 75 08 97 40.
quote: Monday afternoon to Saturday: 10:00am - 12:00pm / 2:00pm - 6:00pm, with Saturday closing at 5:00pm

claim: The Cave de Tain co-op produces the five northern Rhône crus (Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage, Saint-Joseph, Saint-Péray, Cornas); 45-minute guided visits with a 5-wine tasting cost €15/pp and run May–August daily at 10:30 and 15:30 (French) plus 14:30 in English, by reservation.
quote: 5 crus of the Rhône Valley: Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage, Saint-Joseph, Saint-Péray and Cornas… Guided visits last approximately 45 minutes plus a tasting of 5 wines, costing 15€ per person

claim: The most highly regarded Saint-Joseph producers — Gonon, Chave, Coursodon and Gripa — are clustered in the village of Mauves on the right bank just south of Tournon, the so-called 'Gang of Mauves'.
quote: Mauves is famous for well-known producers including Gonon, Chave, Coursodon and Gripa—a group known as the 'Gang of Mauves'

claim: Domaine du Colombier in Mercurol (Florent and David Viale) farms 16 ha of Crozes-Hermitage and Hermitage with a sales cellar open April–October daily 09:30–12:30 / 14:30–19:00.
quote: April to October daily 9:30am to 12:30pm and 2:30pm to 7pm… 16 hectares in Crozes-Hermitage and Hermitage
